03 / THE PACKAGING JOURNEY

Clarity at every stage.
Continuity to the finished piece.

A workflow from brief to handover. The sequence and approval points are agreed around each order’s structure, material and requirements.

  1. 01

    Understand the brief

    Start with the product, how it will be used, estimated quantities and brand goals. Share photographs, dimensions or a reference sample. Missing information is discussed to clarify the scope before a production approach is chosen.

    ✓Agree on requirements & inputs
  2. 02

    Structure & artwork

    Review dimensions, materials, layout and printed content together. Artwork needs to be checked against the packaging structure so important details are not missed. The scope of samples and approvals is agreed for each project before production.

    ✓Confirm artwork & sample scope
  3. 03

    Print to the brief

    The print approach depends on the artwork, material and order requirements. Content, colour and placement are compared with the agreed reference. Particular colour or surface requirements should be clarified during the technical discussion.

    ✓Compare content & print colour
  4. 04

    Form & finish

    Printed sheets move through the stages appropriate to the packaging structure, from forming to assembly and finishing details. Surfaces, folds, joins and accessories are considered together so the finished piece suits the intended use discussed in the brief.

    ✓Review structure & finishing details
  5. 05

    Review the finished piece

    Review finished pieces against the agreed criteria: content, appearance, colour and the usability of the structure. Items needing attention are discussed, sorted and addressed before handover. Any business-specific acceptance requirements should be shared early.

    ✓Compare with approved criteria
  6. 06

    Pack & hand over

    Agree on outer packing, sorting, carton labels and delivery information for the order. Delivery dates and transport arrangements are confirmed individually. Clear handover information helps purchasing and warehouse teams receive and count the finished packaging.

    ✓Confirm packing & delivery arrangements

04 / PROCESS & SLA

Clear commitments.
Measurable standards.

Operational stability, transparent information and the capacity to scale — a foundation for working together on every order.

08written commitments

Shared standards.
A dedicated point of contact.

HotPrint commits to eight SLA indicators in writing, with defined measurement methods and reporting intervals.

Partners above VND 1 billion/month

A dedicated Account Manager and an SLA tailored to your systems.

SLA — Measurable commitments

06Production-defect returnsHotPrint commitmentCompleted within 5 daysMeasurement & frequencyFor defects confirmed to result from internal production.

05 / EQUIPMENT & FINISHING

The right process.
For what your product needs.

See equipment in the real production environment. Discuss what each approach needs to achieve for your packaging.

Sheets & surfaces

From a printed sheet to a brand impression.

Equipment and operators work together as printed sheets move through processing. Surface choices are discussed around the paper, artwork and desired feel.

Discuss: paper, colour expectations and surface finish.

Shape & structure

A structure begins with precision.

Each paper component needs to fit the chosen structure and assembly method. Dimensions, folds and component placement should be reviewed on a sample before confirming production.

Discuss: dimensions, structure and intended use.

Labels & details

Small details. Clear identity.

Label rolls and paper details are considered around the application surface, shape and how they will be used. Discuss practical requirements to choose a suitable specification.

Discuss: application surface, format and method.
